did_you_know.text: Did you know? Gideon camped with his army beside the spring of Harod, while the camp of Midian was north of him, near the hill of Moreh in the valley.
Did you know? The LORD reduced Gideon’s army so that Israel would not claim the victory for themselves, but recognize that the LORD’s hand had saved them.
Did you know? After it was announced that anyone who was afraid or trembling could return home, twenty-two thousand men left the camp, and only ten thousand remained.
Did you know? After the drinking test, only three hundred men remained with Gideon; the rest of the warriors knelt down to drink the water.
Did you know? The three hundred chosen warriors went into battle with trumpets, jars, and torches, while the rest of the people were sent home.
Did you know? The camp of Midian is described as exceedingly numerous: its people were compared to locusts, and their camels were beyond counting, like the grains of sand on the seashore.

Did you know? In the camp of Midian, one soldier told of a dream about a loaf of barley bread tumbling down and overturning a tent; the dream was interpreted as a sign of Gideon’s victory over Midian.
Did you know? Gideon divided the three hundred warriors into three companies, and each man carried a trumpet, an empty jar, and a torch hidden inside the jar.
Did you know? Gideon’s warriors did not charge immediately; instead, each man stood in his place around the camp. The noise, trumpets, and torches caused the camp of Midian to panic and flee.

Did you know? The men of Ephraim captured Oreb and Zeeb, two commanders of Midian. Oreb was killed at the Rock of Oreb, and Zeeb at the Winepress of Zeeb; the names of these places have been preserved in their names.
